historical_references.reference: Oriella was the name of a legendary virgin martyr from the early Christian period. According to hagiography, she was a noblewoman from Syria who was forced into marriage against her will. She feigned madness when her husband attempted to consummate the marriage and was subsequently imprisoned. During her imprisonment, she was visited by an angel who healed her of her feigned madness and restored her sanity. Oriella then confessed her Christian faith to her captors and was put on trial for her beliefs. She was sentenced to death and was martyred by being burned alive in a brazen bull. Her feast day is celebrated on September 14.

Oriella is also mentioned in the Golden Legend, a collection of hagiographies from the late medieval period. The Golden Legend recounts the legend of Oriella as a noblewoman from Syria who was married against her will to a pagan king. When the king was unable to consummate the marriage, Oriella was accused of being a sorceress and was sentenced to death. She was thrown into a burning furnace, but emerged unscathed. The king was converted to Christianity and Oriella was venerated as a saint. Her feast day was celebrated on September 14.
